hints: Think about what makes a virus different from even the smallest bacterial cell - does it have a nucleus, cytoplasm, organelles or a cell wall?
walkthrough:
What all cells have that viruses lack**
Think of a bacterium as a living cell. It has cytoplasm, ribosomes, enzymes for metabolism and a cell surface membrane. A virus has none of these. It is acellular, just a tiny particle that cannot carry out metabolism on its own.

What all viruses do have**
Every virus is built the same simple way: a central core of genetic material, either DNA or RNA, wrapped in a protective outer shell made of protein. That shell is called the capsid, made of subunits called capsomeres. Seeing that combination confirms it is a virus.
Final answer: Nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) core surrounded by a protein coat / capsid.

hints: Recall that disease names and virus names are different - focus on the virus names required by this historical question.
Link smallpox to Vari- and measles to Morbilli-; check your spelling of each required name.
walkthrough:
Smallpox virus**
The virus that causes smallpox is called Variola virus. Variola virus belongs to the genus Orthopoxvirus.

Measles virus**
The virus that causes measles is called Morbillivirus. Learning these two names directly gives the two marks.
Final answer: smallpox - Variola; measles - Morbillivirus.

hints: Start by sorting the pathogen types - is measles caused by bacteria or by a virus, and what type of pathogen does penicillin normally attack?
Recall exactly how penicillin works on bacteria - which structure and which enzyme does it block - then ask if a virus has that target.
walkthrough:
Penicillin is a bacteria-only drug**
Penicillin works by stopping bacteria building their cell walls. It blocks the enzyme transpeptidase that cross-links peptidoglycan, also called murein, in growing bacterial walls. It only works when bacteria are growing and making new wall.

Why a virus has no target**
Measles is caused by Morbillivirus, which is acellular. It has no cell wall, no peptidoglycan and no transpeptidase enzyme. It does not grow by itself. With no wall being built, penicillin has nothing to bind to and nothing to stop, so it cannot treat measles.

Final answer: Penicillin only acts on bacteria. Measles is caused by Morbillivirus which has no cell wall of murein / peptidoglycan and no transpeptidase enzyme for penicillin to inhibit, and is acellular / does not grow.

hints: Think about what HIV does to the immune system and what other infections a person with very low immunity is likely to pick up.
walkthrough:
Antibiotics are not for HIV itself**
HIV is a virus, so antibiotics cannot kill it. But HIV destroys helper T cells and weakens the whole immune system in AIDS.

Treating the extra infections**
That loss of immunity leaves the person prone to other infections, often bacterial infections called secondary or opportunistic infections. Antibiotics are prescribed to kill those bacteria or to prevent them developing.
Final answer: To treat / prevent secondary / opportunistic bacterial infections that occur because immunity is weakened by HIV/AIDS.

hints: Take each bullet in Fig. 2.1 in turn and ask what practical problem it removes - start with no mutation and what that means for making one vaccine last.
Think about why using a live but closely related virus gives a strong, long-lasting immune response without causing smallpox itself.
Consider what freeze-dried and heat stable means for keeping vaccine active in hot countries with no fridges.
Consider what easy to give with little training means for how fast and how widely a global programme can vaccinate people.
walkthrough:
No mutation keeps the same vaccine working**
Because the virus did not mutate, its antigens stayed the same. That means the same vaccine could be used everywhere for many years. No new vaccines, trials or boosters were needed, and people stayed protected for life after vaccination because memory cells still recognised the virus.

Live related virus gives strong safe immunity**
The vaccine used a live virus closely related to smallpox virus. Because it is live it replicates a little, so it presents the same antigens strongly and triggers a strong immune response with memory cells. Because it is not the real smallpox virus it does not cause smallpox, so it is safer to make and give and more people accept it.

Thermostable means it reaches everywhere**
Freeze-dried vaccine is heat stable. It does not degrade easily, has a long shelf-life and needs no refrigeration. That makes storage and transport to hot, remote areas cheap and easy with little wastage.

Easy to give means fast global coverage**
A vaccine that is easy to administer needs little training, so non-medical staff can give it. That makes vaccination faster, cheaper and more accessible, so very high coverage needed for eradication can be achieved.

Final answer: No mutation so same antigens so same vaccine effective everywhere for many years with long-lasting immunity and no need for new research / boosters; live closely related virus replicates giving strong immune response with memory cells but without causing smallpox / fewer safety problems; thermostable so easily stored / transported without refrigeration with long shelf-life and no wastage; easy to administer so rapid high coverage by non-medical staff.

hints: Ask two separate questions - did the person make their own antibodies (active) or receive ready-made antibodies (passive), and did it come from a medical vaccine (artificial) or from catching the disease (natural)?
walkthrough:
Sorting the vaccine immunity**
A vaccine contains antigen, not antibody. The person's own lymphocytes respond, make plasma cells and memory cells and their own antibodies. That is active immunity. Because it was given deliberately by vaccination, it is artificial, not natural. No ready-made antibodies were injected, so it is not passive. So tick active and artificial, cross natural and passive.
Final answer: active immunity - gained (tick); artificial immunity - gained (tick); natural immunity - not gained (cross); passive immunity - not gained (cross).
